title: Define proposed additive Map/Event/Task specification and fixtures
problem: The 0.7.3 vocabulary is scoped in core issue #22, but semantic kinds, relationships, canonical identity and compatibility need one normative implementation contract.
outcome: An immutable proposed 0.7.3 specification, current35-kind index and self-describing semantic fixture corpus, with all legacy parity preserved. This job proves normative producer integrity only; actual new-core parsing/validation/roundtrip/artifact acceptance is the mandatory subsequent j04 consumer gate. key_files: package version metadata and migration documentation
hard_constraints: Document required/optional attributes, canonical ID prefixes, collision scope, relationship legality and examples before implementing each kind. Exact definitions are proposed here, not claimed already ratified.

Distinguish semantic Task from a runtime MCP task handle; semantic Event from a delivered notification; Map from an unvalidated bag of arbitrary objects. Define explicit correlation fields without collapsing identities.
Preserve EventRef as a reference to an external event. Define relationships to Action, Goal, Effect and other kinds; adding a Task atom must never execute work or grant authority.
Keep closed-set validation. Existing 0.7.2 traces remain readable unchanged; a 0.7.2 consumer encountering new kinds gets explicit unsupported-version behavior rather than silent rewriting.
Canonical package/spec are the single source; MCP vendored fallbacks must later be regenerated from this exact reviewed core, never hand-edited. Keep package, grammar and transport versions separate.
Use 0.7.3 candidate metadata consistently without creating tags or publishing packages. Resolve a material semantic policy ambiguity with the operator before proceeding beyond approved scope.
Modify only scholialang-spec in this isolated execution worktree. Related repository semantics are pinned read-only inputs; never mutate sibling/shared checkouts.

Preserve every historical fixture and ID. New semantic kinds must never grant execution authority. Task runtime and semantic state remain distinct. Mark exact additive contract decisions proposed for operator morning review, not already ratified.
Create isolated test/build environments; never pip install into shared control-plane venv. Explicitly prove imported core/spec sources match accepted receipts; sibling-source discovery is not proof.
Final result must include positive and negative conformance tests and immutable evidence. Existing green baseline alone does not establish new feature acceptance.

Follow .ralph/contracts/semantic-contract-proposal.md and .ralph/contracts/spec-first-acceptance-plan.md. The latter defines spec-first producer acceptance versus later actual core consumer acceptance, not a waived parent gate. Preserve all historical 32-kind references/corpora; use a new current projection and phase-aware semantic fixtures. No fake implementation, missing required cases, skip/xfail, or source-discovery leakage.

Write an agent-authored POST with canonical headings exactly: ## What worked, ## What didn't, ## Per-story status, ## Next steps. Record actual observed UTC timestamps and measured test counts; never estimate future completion times or claim tests not collected. Distinguish requested/served model attestation from incidental commit co-author labels. Include exact candidate SHA, source/fixture hashes and unresolved evidence caveats; independent PM acceptance is separate.

Read and verify .ralph/receipts/sch073-j02.json as the fulfilled coordination prerequisite. This job owns normative spec/fixture integrity, not actual new core behavior. Run existing spec tests against exact legacy_core source, current index-driven generation without importing a fictional core, and the complete new fixture integrity matrix. Preserve historical references byte-identically; subsequent j04 owns actual runtime/parser/artifact proof.
